display.purpose: The page thesis, once per page, upper-left, at a 17ch measure. Slight optical tightening (-0.02em).

headline.purpose: Section heads and the closing call, on the canvas.

title.purpose: The question at the top of each session moment, and each setup step. Max 24ch.

body.purpose: Document default, Instrument Sans at 15px with tabular figures on for the whole document. Hero lede 62ch.

body-sm.purpose: The working size: section subheads, moment, step and card prose, table cells, FAQ answers.

panel-title.purpose: The 30px title row of a sheet: the tape title, table captions, the surface index, the boundary columns.

label.purpose: Sentence case, 11px, weight 500, no letter-spacing, in --text-2: column headers, definition terms, the shot bar, the code head, footer column heads, rail ticks.

figures.purpose: Data figures in Instrument Sans with tabular digits (tabular-nums, "tnum" 1): the tape, fact lists, table cells, timestamps.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono, for code only: code blocks, environment strings, inline code and the README cite.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: A floating overlay (the skip link when focused), with the 12px overlay radius and a 1px --panel-border line. The only elevation in the system.

shadows.name: marker-ring
shadows.purpose: A 2px ring in the sheet colour that keeps a specimen marker legible over any pixel of a screenshot. A ring, not elevation.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Chrome state: nav, buttons, segments, the copy button, row hover.

motion.name: motion-base
motion.purpose: Surface state: the disclosure marker rotation, rail tick colour.

motion.name: flash-duration
motion.purpose: A repriced value tints toward --flash-up or --flash-down and fades.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing for every state transition.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entry easing for the pour-in only.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-element delay applied via --d when a group enters together, sorted by top edge so it pours top-to-bottom.

motion.name: rail-fade
motion.purpose: The time rail fading in when the session section enters the reading band.

motion.name: tape-interval
motion.purpose: One value repriced at a time on the live board. Cleared while the tab is hidden; never started under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Disclosure
components.description: FAQ rows on a sheet, ruled with the divider; hover paints the hover fill across the row, and the plus rotates 45 degrees to an accent cross when open.
components.html:
Can Gamma place trades?

No, and it is not a setting. The read-only contract is exposed by the API itself.

Is this investment advice?

No. Gamma is research software.
components.css: .ds-faq { max-width: 800px; border-radius: var(--panel-radius); background: var(--panel-bg); overflow: hidden; font-family: var(--font-ui); } .ds-qa + .ds-qa { border-top: 1px solid var(--divider); } .ds-qa summary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 16px 16px 24px; cursor: pointer; list-style: none; font-size: clamp(0.95rem, 1.3vw, 1.06rem); font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--text-0); transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-qa summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-qa summary:hover { background: var(--hover-bg); } .ds-qa summary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: -2px; } .ds-qa summary .ds-mark { margin-left: auto; margin-right: 4px; flex: none; width: 13px; height: 13px; color: var(--text-2); transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1); } .ds-qa[open] summary .ds-mark { transform: rotate(45deg); color: var(--accent); } .ds-qa .ds-answer { padding: 0 24px 24px; max-width: 70ch; } .ds-qa .ds-answer p { margin: 0; font-size: 13.5px; color: var(--text-1); line-height: 1.7; }

narrative.overview:
The site is a morning of research laid across one plane: a cool, flat canvas with borderless tonal sheets on it, exactly as the application builds a workspace. The canvas carries the page's headings and the hero; everything that holds evidence — the live board, each moment of the session, the surface cells, the boundary, every table, key card, code block and FAQ list, and the footer — is a sheet one tonal step above it, separated by 8px seams or by canvas space between sections. A sheet's edge is its change of tone, never a line. A time rail on the left carries the session's timestamps like the scale on an instrument; it activates only while the session is in view, because a rail that tracked the whole document would be a minimap.

The palette, the type and the shapes are the application's B′ "Tonal compact" tokens, copied value for value into site.css (a static site cannot import the app's stylesheets). There is no marketing-only colour. Both themes come from the same role names and follow the operating system: the site is light when the OS is light and dark when it is dark, which is the app's System default. Instrument Sans is the interface, label and figure font, with tabular figures across the whole document; a monospace appears only where the content is code.

Restraint is enforced by role, not by taste. Chrome is neutral; hue appears only where a value has direction, a state has a name, or an action is the primary one. The refusal the product is built on — Gamma cannot place an order — is given three full sheets with semantic checkmarks and crosses rather than a footnote, and every sample value on the page wears a Mock tag, because a marketing surface that quietly showed synthetic numbers as live would contradict the product it is selling.
keyCharacteristics: A flat cool canvas with borderless tonal sheets on it; no texture, no ruled ground
Light and dark from one set of role names, following the OS (System by default), WCAG AA in both
One accent, for interaction and the primary action only; data supplies the rest of the colour
Instrument Sans everywhere, with tabular figures; JetBrains Mono for code only
Sentence-case labels at 11px, weight 500, no letter-spacing
Filled, edgeless controls; the primary action is an accent tint, never a solid fill
Pill tags with a dot for state; sample data is always tagged
Floating overlays (12px radius and the overlay shadow) are the only elevation
Motion is functional — a pour-in on entry, a sweep that tracks reading position, one board that ticks
Nothing is hidden by an overflow-x mask; wide content scrolls inside its own container

rules.name: The Data-Owns-Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome is neutral. Hue enters only where a value has a direction (positive/negative), a state has a name (live/delayed/mock/planned), or an action is primary. A section heading, a nav item at rest, a sheet and a body paragraph are never coloured.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: --accent is the only chrome accent on the site. The gold is the warning and context role and never a second brand colour. If a new element wants a third colour, it wants a semantic role that already exists.

rules.name: The Labeled-Absence Rule
rules.body: Anything sample, delayed, planned or degraded says so in words and in tone: sample data wears an amber Mock or Sample tag, planned things a neutral tag with a hollow dot, and a degradation note leads with an amber phrase. No synthetic value on this site is ever presented untagged.

rules.name: The Same-Roles-Both-Themes Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a custom property in site.css, defined once in the dark :root block and once in the prefers-color-scheme: light block, with the app's literal values. A rule names a role, never a hex value, so the second theme is never an afterthought. --text-2 reaches 4.5:1 on the sheet and the tint in both themes but not on the light canvas, so text on the canvas uses --text-1 or --text-0.

rules.name: The Two-Type Rule
rules.body: Sans explains the instrument; tabular figures carry the research; mono is for code. The two types are proportional interface text and tabular data figures, both Instrument Sans: the body turns tabular figures on for the whole document, so a number in a table, a fact list, a tag or a sentence holds its width. JetBrains Mono is applied by one short selector list in site.css (code, .code pre, .key .env, .pull cite). Never set chrome or data in a monospace because the product handles numbers; adding a code element means adding it to that list.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels, tags, buttons, tabs and headings are sentence case; the copy carries its own capitals. There is no text-transform: uppercase anywhere in the stylesheet. Upper case appears only where the content is itself a code — environment variables, key names, tickers, tenors — and that content is written in capitals in the markup.

rules.name: The No-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Labels and body text carry no letter-spacing. The only tracking on the site is a slight optical tightening of large type: -0.02em on the display headline and -0.015em on section headlines.

rules.name: The Fluid-Minimum Rule
rules.body: Every auto-placed grid track is written minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr). The min() guarantees the declared minimum never exceeds the viewport, so no grid can push the page wider than the screen; the page has no horizontal overflow at 390px.

rules.name: The No-Mask Rule
rules.body: There is no overflow-x: hidden anywhere in the system. Wide content is given its own scroll container instead — the table sheet, the code block's pre, the live board's tape and segmented track, the nav strip below 860px, and the screenshot frame below 760px (where a 1920px capture becomes a 740px-wide pannable viewport labelled "Drag to pan"). Hiding overflow hides a layout bug; scrolling it admits one honestly.

rules.name: The One-Plane Rule
rules.body: Regions are separated by tone and space, not by borders. A sheet sits on the canvas, a block sits on the tint inside a sheet, and rules (--divider) divide rows inside them. A line around a region turns the plane back into outlined boxes.

rules.name: The Overlays-Only Rule
rules.body: Only a floating overlay may cast a shadow. Everything else conveys depth with a tonal step. A shadow, glow or blur on a sheet, button, tag, card or table is out of system, and so is glass.

rules.name: The Visible-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: .reveal resolves to opacity: 1. The pour-in — a 620ms rise from 15px — is applied by adding a class on intersection, and only inside a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference block on a .js root. A failed observer, a disabled script, or a reduced-motion preference costs the animation and never the copy. Elements entering together are sorted by their top edge and staggered 55ms apart via a --d custom property, so a group pours top-to-bottom rather than arriving at once.

dos: Do copy colours from the app's tokens.css into the two token blocks in site.css, by role, for both themes. This site has no marketing-only colour, and adding one would break the claim that the screenshots and the page are the same world.
Do check every change in the light and the dark theme, and keep text at 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24px, or 18.66px bold) over its rendered background in both.
Do put evidence on a sheet (--panel-bg, 6px, no edge) and inner blocks on the tint; separate related sheets with 8px seams.
Do write labels in sentence case at 11px / 500 in --text-2, with no letter-spacing, and let the copy carry its own capitals.
Do set every number in Instrument Sans with tabular figures, and keep JetBrains Mono for code by adding a code element to the mono selector list.
Do fill every action: --button-bg for ordinary buttons, --tint for a ghost, the accent tint for the one primary action.
Do write auto-placed grid tracks as minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr).
Do give wide content its own scroll container, and label it when the gesture is not obvious (the screenshot frame's "Drag to pan" below 760px).
Do tag every synthetic value Mock (or Sample) and every planned provider with the hollow-dot tag, on this site as in the app.
Do annotate a screenshot with a numbered .mark-pt plus a legend row, and keep the marker pointer-events: none.
Do keep .reveal's resting state visible and animate only on entry.
donts: Don't draw a border around a sheet, card, block, field, tag or button; the tonal step is the edge. Lines are for row rules, the selected segment, hover, focus and the primary action's edge.
Don't put a shadow, glow or blur on anything but a floating overlay.
Don't add texture to the canvas — no grid, no grain, no ruled ground.
Don't use a radius off the scale (5px controls, 6px sheets and blocks, 12px overlays, pills for tags only), or a circle for anything that is not a dot or a numbered marker.
Don't colour chrome. A heading, a nav item at rest, a sheet or a body paragraph is neutral; hue belongs to values, states and the one primary action.
Don't fill a button with a solid accent, green or red.
Don't uppercase or track a label, or write copy in capitals; upper case is for content that is itself a code.
Don't set chrome, labels or figures in a monospace, or set figures in proportional digits.
Don't put --text-2 on the light canvas; it is tuned for the sheet and the tint.
Don't add overflow-x: hidden anywhere. If something overflows, either fix the track minimum or give it a scroll container.
Don't float a callout over a screenshot. The marker points; the legend explains.
Don't let the time rail track the whole document or appear below 1180px — it belongs to the session section and needs its own 92px column.
Don't hide content behind a scroll-triggered animation. If the observer never fires, the page must still read completely.
Don't show a number on this site that a real Gamma surface could not produce, and never show one without its provenance or its Mock tag.
